Container.Name: Mnema-Talk
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: chat voice video screen share talk team community self-hosted
Container.Overview: Your own place to hang out: text channels, drop-in voice Talks, video and screen sharing up to 4K at 60 FPS. One small self-hosted server for one community, on your own hardware, with your data staying with you. This template installs the whole stack in one go: Mnema Talk, PostgreSQL and SeaweedFS (media storage). Needs Unraid 8 or newer. Put a reverse proxy with HTTPS in front (for example Nginx Proxy Manager) and forward the voice ports on your router. Full guide: https://github.com/mnema-xyz/talk/blob/main/doc/unraid.md
Container.Description:
Mnema Talk is a small, self-hosted home for one community.
- Text channels, threads, DMs, polls, events and a wiki - Drop-in voice Talks, video and screen share up to 4K at 60 FPS - Web app, desktop app and bots, one Go binary - Runs fine on a NAS: Mnema Talk + PostgreSQL + SeaweedFS, installed together
**Before you start:** you need a domain with HTTPS (reverse proxy) and three router forwards (HTTPS, the UDP voice range 50000-50050 and port 3479 UDP and TCP). Never forward the web port itself. Generate each secret below with `openssl rand -hex 32`.

Config.Name: Public URL
Config.Description: The address people open in their browser, with https://. Required.

Config.Name: Web UI port
Config.Description: Port of the web app on this server. Point your reverse proxy at it. Never forward it on your router.

Config.Name: Voice UDP port min
Config.Description: First port of the UDP range for voice, video and screen share. Forward the range on your router.

Config.Name: Voice UDP port max
Config.Description: Last port of the UDP range.

Config.Name: Voice relay port
Config.Description: Relay for members whose network blocks the UDP range (UDP and TCP). Forward it on your router.

Config.Name: Appdata path
Config.Description: Where PostgreSQL and the media store keep their data. A cache-only path (for example /mnt/cache/appdata/mnema-talk) is faster for the database.

Config.Name: Admin username
Config.Description: Name of the first admin account, created on the first start.

Config.Name: Admin password
Config.Description: Password of the first admin account. Used once, on the first start; change it after you log in. Required.

Config.Name: JWT secret
Config.Description: Signs login sessions. Required: paste the output of openssl rand -hex 32. Keep it; changing it logs everyone out.

Config.Name: Database password
Config.Description: Password of the PostgreSQL user. Required: paste the output of openssl rand -hex 32. Set it before the first start; it cannot be changed afterwards by editing this field.

Config.Name: Media storage secret
Config.Description: Secret key of the media store. Required: letters and digits only, at least 8 characters, e.g. openssl rand -hex 32.

Config.Name: Language
Config.Description: Default language of the server: en or de.

Config.Name: Reverse proxy address
Config.Description: Address of your reverse proxy container (for example 172.17.0.5), so real visitor addresses reach the server. One address, never a whole range.

Config.Name: Public IP or DynDNS name
Config.Description: Only if voice does not connect from outside: your public IP or DynamicDNS name. Empty = detected automatically.

Config.Name: Max upload (MB)
Config.Description: Largest file a member can upload.

Config.Name: SMTP host
Config.Description: Outgoing mail server for address confirmation and password reset. Empty = no e-mail.

Config.Name: SMTP port
Config.Description: Usually 587 (starttls) or 465 (tls).

Config.Name: SMTP username
Config.Description: Mail account name.

Config.Name: SMTP password
Config.Description: Mail account password.

Config.Name: SMTP from
Config.Description: Sender address, for example talk@example.com.
